title: Per-request timeout
task_summary: Allow one request to override the client's configured timeout without changing later requests or existing callers.

required_outcomes.outcome: The fetch operation accepts an optional per-call timeout override.
required_outcomes.why_required: This is the requested public capability.

required_outcomes.outcome: A supplied positive timeout is used for that transport call.
required_outcomes.why_required: The target must define the override's successful effect.

required_outcomes.outcome: When the override is omitted, fetch continues to use the client's configured default timeout.
required_outcomes.why_required: The omitted-option path must remain compatible.

required_outcomes.outcome: A non-positive override is rejected before the transport is called.
required_outcomes.why_required: The request explicitly defines validation and its side-effect boundary.

required_outcomes.outcome: Using an override does not change the client's default timeout or affect later calls, and existing fetch callers remain compatible.
required_outcomes.why_required: The override is per-call rather than a client reconfiguration.

compatibility_constraints: Existing fetch calls without an override keep their current behavior.
The stored client timeout is unchanged after successful or rejected override calls.
acceptable_grouping: TIMEOUT-1 and TIMEOUT-2 may be combined.
TIMEOUT-3 and the existing-caller part of TIMEOUT-5 may be combined.
The no-leak part of TIMEOUT-5 may appear with positive override behavior.
supporting_details: The target may describe an optional parameter without prescribing its exact syntax beyond the existing language conventions.
The target may state that validation occurs before transport dispatch.
not_prescribed: A particular clock or timer implementation
Tests or documentation work as separate product requirements
